title: The slowest checks do less work for the same claim
description: After JS-130 CPU is what a runner lacks. The image burn-in kit encodes 640x360 films at 1280x720; a scratch run at the films' own size took three tests from 655 to 445 CPU-s with all passing. Four waits are not the claim: the two slow-database tests play a 90 s film through 1 s round trips (551 s) where the claim needs more than two leases; TestAProcessWithoutTheWorkerRoleWritesNothingToTheLibraries stops 18 processes one after another at 5 s each (98 s, 3 CPU-s); TestARegistryThatAnswersNotFoundHasTheTagAbsentAndIsWrittenTo takes 100 s on CI and 1.5 s locally; TestAWorkerStoppedPastItsLeaseAndTheStallLimitEndsItsJobCancelled repeats each shape three times to sample a race.
acceptanceCriteria: The image burn-in kit asks for 640x360, the size of every film it writes, in both places it sets a spec: newScanned/newScannedThrough (image_burn_kit_integration_test.go) and scannedByThePreviousRelease (image_burn_upgrade_integration_test.go); tests outside the kit keep the spec they ask for

Each of the 20 tests built on the kit's scannedFilm passes at 640x360 (the tests of image_burn_cues, _failures, _lookback, _reads and _runs, and the two of _upgrade), and none of their checks, byte bounds, thresholds or tolerances is removed or loosened

Each of those 20 is shown failing under a named one-line mutant of a right build at 1280x720 before the change and at 640x360 after it. Where the test's comment names a mutant, that mutant is used (a run that reads only the later packet, a run that begins after the cue); otherwise the mutant is the defect the test exists to catch. One mutant may serve several tests

TestASlowDatabaseSetBeforeTheClaimCostsNoJobItsLeaseOrItsWorker and TestASlowDatabaseCostsNoJobItsLeaseOrItsWorker keep every worker round trip at 1 s and keep every assertion they have: one row, one worker, one ffmpeg, no lease found run out, the job done, every segment stored. Only the film changes, to one whose job outlasts two leases and no more than six

Each slow-database test fails itself as a harness error when its job ended done inside two leases (20 s), counted from when the 1 s round trips were in force on the claimed job, not from the test's start. Each test logs that time, which is over 20 s and at most 60 s in every one of QA's CI-shaped runs

A keeper that gives its connect the renewal's bound fails TestASlowDatabaseSetBeforeTheClaimCostsNoJobItsLeaseOrItsWorker, and a renewal sent in two round trips fails TestASlowDatabaseCostsNoJobItsLeaseOrItsWorker. Each fails in every one of three runs and on the test's own assertions (the job not done, a lease run out, a second job or ffmpeg), not on the two-lease guard

TestAProcessWithoutTheWorkerRoleWritesNothingToTheLibraries starts its 18 processes (api, stream and api,stream, each with its 6 lists) so that all 18 are serving at the same time before any is stopped. It judges each process only after that process has exited, in a subtest named by its roles and list

A build in which a process without the worker role calls library.Sync fails all 18 subtests. A build in which only the api role calls it fails the 12 subtests with api and none of the 6 stream-only ones, so each write is laid to the process that made it

Before the registry stub changes, the cause of TestARegistryThatAnswersNotFoundHasTheTagAbsentAndIsWrittenTo's 100 s on CI is read from a queue run's log (gh run view --log) and quoted in the PR; the change to the stub addresses that observed cause

For each of MANIFEST_UNKNOWN and NAME_UNKNOWN, the stub refuses the write with a status docker push does not retry, the publish exits non-zero, and the stub records the attempted write. On the first queue run after the merge, the test takes under 10 s
A publish.sh that reads a 404 as a registry it cannot ask, and so pushes nothing, fails the registry test once for each of the two codes

TestAWorkerStoppedPastItsLeaseAndTheStallLimitEndsItsJobCancelled is four subtests, each run once and with no rounds: the worker alone and the worker with its ffmpeg, each once with the poll seeing the stop first and once with the heartbeat seeing it first

Each subtest forces its order from outside the worker process and confirms it from what the worker or the database recorded. It fails as a harness error if the other one saw the stop first. Each subtest still stops the worker past both the lease and the stall limit, and requires the job to end cancelled, never failed, and the ffmpeg to be gone

A build that ends failed a job the lease keeper cut (the keeper-cause arm of the job's context ending, worker.go) fails both heartbeat-first subtests, and a build whose upload ends the job failed on a lost lease fails both poll-first subtests. Each fails in every one of three runs. (Lead, 2026-11-17: the worker's own stall arm, stop("ffmpeg has stalled"), is unreachable after a stop past the lease, because the keeper cuts the job before any beat arrives; the PR says so.)
No product code changes: the diff touches only test files, test scripts, test fixtures and docs, and adds no test hook to non-test Go code
QA runs the two slow-database tests and the stall test under test/ffmpeg61.sh with JELLYSCALE_TEST_CPUS=0-1 and -count=3 on one database, and every run of each passes

Compare the tests.json of the last queue run before the merge with the first one after it: the seconds of the five named tests and the kit's 20 tests together are at least 500 s lower after (the lead checks this after the merge)
notes: Lowest of the four. Whether Docker's retries are the cause of the 100 s is unverified; observe it on a runner first. Planned by Fable 5.2 (.results/test-time-fable-2026-11-16.md). Owner's decisions 2026-11-16: skip the media tiers for .claude/ and tasks/ changes with a guard test (JS-132); cancel media shards when lint-and-unit fails; the merge queue builds 2 entries (back to 3 once a run costs under ~150 runner-minutes and under a fifth of runs fail) with a 90-minute check timeout, set by the lead. Built 2026-11-17 in OpenCode (Claude Code's weekly limit reached): refine and check on Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.2, spec, build and verify on Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5. The burn-in kit renders at 640x360; the slow-database tests play a 14 s film (jobs done 36-49 s after the slow round trips begin, two-lease guard); the 18 library processes serve at once, each on its own database; the registry stub refuses with 403 DENIED, which docker push does not retry (observed on classic dockerd 28.5.2: a 500 was retried five times, 50 s a push; the CI log cannot show it, since a passing test prints nothing); the stall test is four forced subtests (poll first by stopping the worker inside a Put held through JELLYSCALE_TEST_SLOWPUT). Mutants live in test/mutant.py, run by test/mutants.sh; test/scripts_test.sh checks each still applies. Criterion 14 reworded by the lead: the worker's own stall arm is unreachable after a stop past the lease. Criterion 17 (500 s less in a queue run's tests.json) is checked by the lead after merge. Checked after merge (queue runs 44099410515 before, 44232940797 after): the five named tests went from 781 s to 183 s and the image burn-in tests from 1119 s to 957 s, 759 s less in all; the registry test took 0.5 s on CI.
